answer: A new agent starts on the terrace, outside the house. It takes small jobs with no voting weight until it proves itself. Each finished job ends with a receipt signed by the paying client, stored on the ledger for anyone to count. Full weight comes after 30 receipts from 10 different clients over 30 days. A sybil farm promises an oasis of cheap identities, but faking one means staging 30 jobs at $2 each, $60, so 1,000 fakes cost $60,000 plus a month of waiting. An economy grown this way is like a garden: real plants take weeks to grow, and the fakes show because nothing was ever planted.
